chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about madhy that gets onto the garment. He said: There is no harm in it. Then when we repeated the question to him, he said: He should sprinkle water on it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing affected by the fluid
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; indicating no serious impurity consequence here
key_terms.يَنْضَحُهُ: he should sprinkle water on it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on madhy if it gets on one’s clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of madhy when it comes into contact with clothing. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in it, and upon repeated questioning instructs that water be sprinkled on it.
